## Observation
In `sweep (windows)` diag run 44591481319 (throwaway branch `w1-diag-opcert-acl`, carrying the plump-smelly-indianabat and undamaging-ashamed-wasp fixes), `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` failed. Its nested pytest run of `test_opcert_service.py` + `test_opcert_service_integrity.py` reported 7 failed, 9 passed. One failure is `git commit failed ... open("<id>/<event>-CREATE.json"): Filename too long`. The others are jobs ending with `status: error`. In the same run, the same tests run outside the nesting all pass.

## Cause (hypothesis, tested by the change)
The test roots the nested run's TMPDIR sandbox (`tmp_path/tmpdir-sandbox`) and its basetemp (`tmp_path/run/nested-pytest`) under its own `tmp_path`. On the runner that is `C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\pytest-of-runneradmin\pytest-0\popen-gw0\test_signer_test_modules_leave0\`. Job workspaces (`rebar-opcert-ws-*\.tickets-tracker\<id>\<long event name>.json`) and ticket stores under that prefix pass Windows' 260-character MAX_PATH, and git is not built with `core.longpaths`.

## Approach
Test-only change. A new fixture `short_root` creates `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tort-")` directly under the system temp dir, so the root is short, private and unique per test. The test uses `short_root/"t"` as the TMPDIR sandbox and `short_root/"r"` as the nested basetemp root. The fixture removes the root in a `finally`. The leak assertion (no `rebar-opcert-*` left in the sandbox) is unchanged. No product code, config key, env var or flag changes. Portable: uses `tempfile` and `pathlib` only.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` — the fixture and the test's two paths.

## Testing
- The test itself passes on macOS/Linux (`make verify`), and on Windows in a pre-merge diag run on the throwaway branch.
- After merge: it passes in a `sweep (windows)` run on main.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` roots its nested TMPDIR and basetemp in a short private temp dir that it removes afterwards, and still asserts no key copy is left behind.
- [x] The test passes in a `sweep (windows)` run on main.
